about: scripts/opcount: the program mode builds the Ergo side as the product does (ergo's patched release, each package's IR read with -ergoir, through build.Toolchain.Command) and reports per package how many function bodies came from IR. The ergo build -work / -go-text choice and the runs are checked by hand (OPCOUNT-IR round-1 request: opcount station-stats on both paths), not by a gate test: they build ergo and run Go.

mutants.name: opcount-ir-flag-dropped
mutants.origin: wf10 OPCOUNT-IR (C0b: opcount could not build an IR module)
mutants.rule: Each package of the emitted module that has an IR file compiles with its own -ergoir, as ergo build compiles it.

mutants.name: opcount-stock-go
mutants.rule: The program builds with the release ergo builds with and its patched compile, the only compile that reads -ergoir.

mutants.name: opcount-overlay-dropped
mutants.rule: The measured binary carries the exit hook, added by the overlay.

mutants.name: opcount-bodies-ir-uncounted
mutants.rule: A package's IR count is the functions its IR file names.

mutants.name: opcount-bodies-runtime-counted
mutants.rule: The runtime's nested module is no package of the program: its functions are not counted.
